reason: Plugin config is declared as a Go struct with defaults, tag constraints and a Validate method, checked through the cordis port's Schema interface; the vendored, locally patched schema builder is not ported.

Wire messages, persisted records, projection state and tool input are Go types; their JSON Schema, validation and strict decoding come from one harness schema package over github.com/google/jsonschema-go instead of hand-written zod schemas.

Its one runtime job, checking literal defaults against a generated JSON Schema, and its test job, validating generated documents, are done by the same module that derives the schemas, so no separate validator is needed.

The types-only agreement that lets cordis accept any schema library is expressed by the existing cordis.Schema Go interface and ConfigError type in the cordis port; no package of shared type definitions is needed.

Compilation and type checking are done by the Go toolchain; the compiler-API uses (type-graph generation, persistence fingerprints, catalogs) are replaced by reflection at startup and the standard library's Go parser and type checker.

It exists only to write a declaration source map for a TypeScript declaration file generated by the upstream build (typert.remote-client.d.ts); the Go design generates no declaration files, so there is nothing to map.
The override forces every consumer onto a vendored, locally modified schema library; the Go design vendors and forks no schema library because config shapes are Go types.

title: Five schema systems coexist (schemastery, zod, the in-house tool schema language, typert-generated zod, ajv) joined by four lossy converters

reason: A shape is declared once as a Go type and converted into exactly one derived form, JSON Schema, by one module, so there is no converter between schema libraries.

title: Each data shape is written twice, as a TypeScript interface and as a runtime schema, cross-checked by a generator and bridged by casts

reason: The Go type is the only declaration and the schema is derived from it by reflection, so no second declaration exists to cross-check or cast.

title: schemastery is imported under the name z, which is zod's export name; files needing both rename zod

reason: With one mechanism based on Go types there is no schema-building vocabulary from two libraries to collide.

title: zod is pinned to one exact version in 99 manifests and coupled to third-party SDK peers, so an upgrade is repository-wide

reason: The one schema module is imported by a single harness package, so a version change touches one go.mod line and one package.

title: The Standard Schema interface leaks: the loader detects schemastery by vendor string, a plugin overwrites the property to add a rule, and async validation is a rejected TODO

reason: Field metadata is read from the Go config type by reflection and never through the schema interface, cross-field rules are a Validate method, and the Go interface is synchronous by signature.

title: schemastery is a hand-synced fork with local modifications, process-global counters, callbacks revived with new Function, and validation that mutates its input

reason: Nothing is forked; a derived schema is immutable data without callbacks and decoding never writes into its input.

title: The config JSON Schema is a lossy translation of schemastery with recorded limitations; a validator and a regex parser are loaded only to patch gaps in the translation

reason: The JSON Schema document is derived from the same Go type that config is decoded into, so there is no translation step and defaults are checked when the schema is derived.

title: Erased types force a 9,544-line build-time type-graph generator and a separate fingerprint extractor, with stale-output guards and a widened compiler peer range

reason: Go types are available at run time through reflection, so schemas and fingerprints are computed in the running program and no generated artifact exists to go stale.

Go toolchain, reflect and go/ast in place of the TypeScript compiler and compiler API
Declaration source maps (not needed: no generated declarations)
The Go type is the only declaration of a data shape
JSON Schema is the one derived form, handled by one module
Defaults are a Go value; input is decoded on top of it
Reflection at startup replaces build-time type-graph generation
A live config field is a tag and an update callback, not a wrapper type
Every registered shape is declared once, described and has parseable tags
Schema derivation succeeds for every registered type and is byte-stable
A tool schema outside the model-facing subset fails registration with all paths
Invalid tool arguments never reach the tool body and all violations are returned
Strict decoding at trust boundaries, with an explicit tolerant mode
Decode onto defaults; derived default annotations; invalid default fails derivation
Validate method errors and defined scalar types report field paths
Discriminated unions derive to oneOf and decode to the right Go type
Fingerprints are stable under reordering and change with the wire shape; golden inventory
Exported schema documents are valid draft 2020-12 and loaded schemas are inert data
Config is checked before the component body; rejection is isolated and never repaired
Live-only config edits update in place; other edits restart
Config write-back omits values equal to defaults and round-trips
Derived config schema carries the metadata the settings UI needs
External JSON Schema documents validate values or are refused with a reason
cordis checks config through one interface without importing its implementation
An optional tool argument that is null or unused does not fail the call; a used value is still validated
Clean checkout builds with the Go toolchain alone; registered types expose schemas without generation
Source-reading tools use the standard library parser and type checker
